scope: Selected original-PDF full-main-body review of planar constrained vehicle barriers, ego-motion-aware target estimation, and lateral-longitudinal coupling. Includes two-paper coupling addendum; no manuscript revision or experiment reproduction.
source_method: Read-only Zotero Desktop local API; attached local original PDFs; pdftotext with page breaks; selected original page renders.

reviewed_sources.title: High-Order Control Barrier Functions
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Xiao and Belta - 2022 - High-Order Control Barrier Functions.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pp1-8 all sections, proofs and references.
findings: Definition8 Eq13 includes sup over admissible U on intersection C1...Cm; Theorem4 requires initial state in all derivative-defined sets and controller satisfying final inequality for all time. Raw distance is seed, not a first-order CBF merely by writing inequality.
Remark1 boundary b=0 and bdot<0 cannot satisfy first derivative barrier for any class-K tuning. Direct formal support for independently derived planar example.

Theorem5 and Corollary1 provide sufficient conditions for input compatibility; penalty adjustment also changes admissible initial set. SecIVB parameterization seeks feasible designs offline; not universal arbitrary-state guarantee.

SecVB is DIRECT bounded-input planar unicycle example, not just longitudinal ACC: yaw-rate limit .2rad/s, accel .5m/s2, speed0..2m/s, squared-distance second-order HOCBF plus speed/CLFs. Supports distinction between position-only first-order failure and legitimate distance-seeded HOCBF.
Remark8 explicitly warns sampled implementation may lose safety between sample instants. Do not assert HOCBF framework intrinsically ignores actuation bounds.

reviewed_sources.title: Obstacle Avoidance for Low-Speed Autonomous Vehicles With Barrier Function
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Chen et al. - 2018 - Obstacle Avoidance for Low-Speed Autonomous Vehicles With Barrier Function.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pages1-13 including AppendicesA-L and proofs.
findings: Acceleration/yaw-rate unicycle, speed/yaw/acceleration/friction constraints Eq3 and Eq39. Relative 4D state includes positions,speed,bearing. Constructs avoidable set via polar algorithm before reciprocal facet barriers Eq40 and mixed-integer disjunction Eq44. Genuine input/dynamics-aware alternative, not naive rawdistance.

Safety definition is passive-friendly responsibility Eq8: stopped-vehicle contact and rear contact excluded. Accurate full state sensing assumed p2. Bounded adversarial pedestrian speed Eq9. Do not advertise theorem as unconditional physical noncollision.

SectionVA infeasible set uses braking only and grid convex hull, intentionally conservative relative to steering options. p7 multiple-obstacle filter may become infeasible; common emergency braking fallback preserves defined passive safety outside braking infeasible sets.

AppendixH sampled inequality derived assuming state derivative constant within interval EqA32, despite nonlinear original dynamics; no general exact intersample certificate established by that Taylor derivation.
1000 trials compare polar/HJ/potential field, not our simulations. No reproduction performed.

reviewed_sources.title: Simultaneous Lane-Keeping and Obstacle Avoidance by Combining Model Predictive Control and Control Barrier Functions
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Bruggemann et al. - 2022 - Simultaneous Lane-Keeping and Obstacle Avoidance by Combining Model Predictive Control and Control B.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pages 1-6, all main sections and references.
findings: Constant longitudinal speed, linear lateral bicycle model and nonlinear global position mapping; steering bounded. Relative degree two explicitly identified pp2-3.

Lane/obstacle deforming barriers, not raw circular distance; exponential and prescribed-time backstepping. Lemma1 assumes nonzero decoupling coefficient everywhere in safe domain, symmetric gains and positive left-lane expansion Eq13. p3 admits coefficients can vanish.

Lemma1 feasible QP optimizes over R, so unbounded-control control-sharing is not physical steering-bound feasibility. ICCBF SecIII-D further restricts set and requires sup over |u|<=umax Eq18; validating it hard, finite successful iteration count open, combined PTSf-ICCBF theory outside scope.

SectionV simulations use ev=0 despite positive expansion assumption in proof. Late obstacle15m at20m/s, steering5deg: saturating non-input-aware safety filter causes collision, ICCBF counterpart avoids in the reported case. Direct 2D evidence supporting bounded-input critique.
Sensing, computing and acquisition beyond scope. Conclusion ongoing research for theoretical guarantees of combined variants.

reviewed_sources.title: Rule-Based Safety-Critical Control Design using Control Barrier Functions with Application to Autonomous Lane Change
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: He et al. - 2021 - Rule-Based Safety-Critical Control Design using Control Barrier Functions with Application to Autono.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pp1-8 including discussion, tables and references.
findings: Small-sideslip CG kinematic bicycle: direct beta affects translational velocity Eq2; cannot transplant rear-axle unicycle relative-degree calculation unchanged. Input and beta-rate constraints TableIII.
Barrier constraints Eq11-13 include time headway and relative-speed-squared braking-distance terms; abort-state lateral clearance is piecewise. NOT simply raw Euclidean distance.
Uses FSM switches on QP solvability; safe switching requires membership in both safe sets. No blanket all-state bounded-input recursive feasibility result established by general CBF preliminaries.

TableVI infeasible fractions .48% urban and .20% highway, but paper attributes failures to unphysical surrounding cars passing through each other and consequent selected-target/barrier discontinuity. Must not relabel as proof of actuator-induced infeasibility.
Remark2 accurate surrounding state data; SecV explicitly assumes exact perception/no delay and leaves state estimator/noisy-distance safety margin and communication delay to future work.

reviewed_sources.title: Safety-Critical Control With Nonaffine Control Inputs Via a Relaxed Control Barrier Function for an Autonomous Vehicle
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Seo et al. - 2022 - Safety-Critical Control With Nonaffine Control Inputs Via a Relaxed Control Barrier Function for an.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pages1-8 including singular-perturbation proof and both experiments.
findings: Nonaffine dynamic bicycle with flat output and dynamic-inversion control. CBF relaxed into penalty. Theorem1/Remark1 guarantee enlarged h>=-mu rather than exact h>=0.
Numerical lane-change safety function is speed limit h=vs^2-vx^2 p4; CarMaker front-car/cut-in uses h=D-0.5*ydot1 p7 (longitudinal time-headway). NOT a pure planar distance obstacle CBF example.

Parameter tr in[-1,1] modeled, but DI update Eq17 has no explicit displayed projection/invariance of bounded input set. Assumption1 requires invertibility and exact tracking solution existence. No need claim theorem false to establish restricted scope.
Full-state sensor info in CarMaker p7, relaxed barrier and discretization admit small violations p7. Exclude as direct counterexample to user planar-distance claim.

reviewed_sources.title: Turning Circle-Based Control Barrier Function for Efficient Collision Avoidance of Nonholonomic Vehicles
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Lee et al. - 2026 - Turning Circle-Based Control Barrier Function for Efficient Collision Avoidance of Nonholonomic Vehi.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pages 1-8, including geometric proof, MPC, experiments and conclusion; pages 4-5 reread after initial tool truncation.
findings: Eq5 acceleration/yaw-rate unicycle with speed state; bounded yaw-rate. Eq6 raw Euclidean clearance is seed; Eq7 ED comparator is hdot+alpha*h, not a position-only first-order barrier. Remark1 explicitly calls it second-order.

TC geometry incorporates turning radius R=u/rmax and smooth underapproximation of max(left,right clearances). Proposition1 gives a fixed turning-circle safety witness for static obstacle, constant speed and instant saturated yaw-rate; this is not a recursive-feasibility proof for the full rate-constrained, moving-obstacle MPC.
MPC Eq13 has state/input/rate constraints and discrete barrier over finite horizon; terminal cost but no displayed invariant terminal-set constraint. Constant-velocity obstacle predictions.
ASV hardware rather than road-car hardware. Remark2 says robust tube tightening is future. Conclusion excludes noise/delay and calls for more rigorous mathematical formulation beyond geometry.

reviewed_sources.title: A Collision Cone Approach for Control Barrier Functions
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Tayal et al. - 2026 - A Collision Cone Approach for Control Barrier Functions.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Original PDF main body and AppendicesA-C pp1-12 read in full; pp13-14 reference/biography pages not substantive review scope.
findings: Unicycle acceleration and angular acceleration; bicycle small-slip affine CG model; obstacle constant-velocity assumptions Theorems1-2. Collision-cone h uses relative position AND velocity.

SectionII-C p1300 explicitly optimizes over R^m and states infinite control authority, leaving input limits future; conclusion p1307 confirms no input limits in simulations and high-speed hardware failures from saturation. Strong direct bounded-input caveat, not a naive-position-only example.

Theorem2 validity on C rather than whole D; unicycle proof referred to earlier source, not supplied here; source was not independently read. AppendixA bicycle uses approximated relative velocity unequal to actual position derivative p1301, conservative radius and small-beta assumptions.

Remark2 p1303 single-obstacle guarantees; conflicting multiobstacle cones and perception-boundary selection theory left future. Stopping fallback in conclusion is not unconditional noncollision against moving obstacles.
Motion capture used in ground experiments, EKF described for quadrotor. Neither justifies claiming all works ignore estimation altogether.

reviewed_sources.title: Future-Focused Control Barrier Functions for Autonomous Vehicle Control
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Black et al. - 2023 - Future-Focused Control Barrier Functions for Autonomous Vehicle Control.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pp1-8 including appendix and experiments.
findings: Dynamically extended kinematic bicycle with slip-angle rate and acceleration inputs Eq8. ff-CBF uses minimum predicted distance under constant-velocity surrogate, not just current distance. Assumption1 excludes initially predicted collisions over horizon.

Theorem1 proves regularity and relation to physical barrier, not bounded-input existence. p5 explicitly states valid CBF IF admissible-input sup condition holds. Theorem2 assumes feasible boundary condition for all time.

Centralized simulations optimize acceleration with bounds; turning nominal clipped separately. ff-CBF 96.3% feasibility one-left-turn, relaxed version100% in1000 trials. p6 explicitly leaves theoretical feasibility guarantees future.
Hardware uses Vicon and PX4 EKF; cannot claim no state estimation considered. No propagated deterministic tracking-error tube in safety theorem is provided in examined formulation.

Constant zero-input surrogate generally still curves for nonzero slip in Eq8, whereas distance prediction assumes straight constant velocity; do not claim constant-input kinematic trajectory equivalence generally.

reviewed_sources.title: Safety-Critical Model Predictive Control with Discrete-Time Control Barrier Function
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Zeng et al. - 2021 - Safety-Critical Model Predictive Control with Discrete-Time Control Barrier Function.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original arXiv v3 PDF pp1-9 including racing appendix.
findings: Discrete barrier Eq10f plus bounded-input MPC; raw quadratic-distance obstacle h Eq17 and quartic shape h Eq21; discrete setting is not the continuous first-order derivative test.

SecIIIC feasibility analysis qualitative; Remark4 p5 explicitly says fixed decay parameter generally provides pointwise feasibility and persistent feasibility remains open. Generic terminal-set symbol does not by itself construct a suitable terminal safe policy.

2D double integrator example is not nonholonomic; racing example uses lateral dynamic model with regressed linear prediction, perfect position estimates explicitly assumed p8, other cars constant lateral offset/speed.
A proof of safety under indefinitely feasible exact discrete constraints must be separated from recursive feasibility, model mismatch and continuous intersample safety.

reviewed_sources.title: Simultaneous ego-vehicle state estimation and vehicle trajectory tracking using a multistage high gain observer
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Sharma et al. - 2026 - Simultaneous ego-vehicle state estimation and vehicle trajectory tracking using a multistage high ga.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original published PDF pp1-20 including derivations, observer conditions, experiment discussion, tables and references.
findings: Eqs9-12 derive rotating-ego relative-position terms and quantify mismatch from misusing inertial dynamics as relative dynamics. Eq15 shows inertial-converted measurement error scaling with ego pose error and range.

NRMM Eq16-18 uses relative position/heading but absolute target speed/acceleration/slip, body ego velocities and yaw-rate. Motion-model Eq17 assumes target acceleration and sideslip constant; this is a model class, not arbitrary unknown maneuver coverage.

Assumption1 p6 sets measured BODY acceleration derivatives adotx=adoty=0 and yaw-rate derivative udot3=0. Eqs24-25 still have nonzero inertial jerk during turning; do not paraphrase as zero inertial jerk. NRMM companion derivation uses this again p10.

Lipschitz calculation pp11-12 freezes ego and target yaw rates; do not reuse constant-rate partial Jacobian as uniform certificate over arbitrary maneuvering domain. Need project-specific validated domains/derivatives.

Theorem1 nominal exponential observer result; yaw observer Theorem2 H-infinity L2 attenuation does not supply a deterministic pointwise collision tube automatically. Position/velocity chart has divisions by target speed squared.

Full-scale road data (not closed-loop evasive collision-avoidance control), two highway cases and RMM near-relative-zero failure; Table3 NRMM not best in every metric: InMM absolute-speed RMS .24 vs NRMM .41; RMM course RMS1.12 vsNRMM1.19deg. Do not repeat blanket superiority.

Alai2024 provides same relative-model antecedent; NRMM not proved unique necessary model. Any consistent relative or properly transformed inertial model with certified errors could in principle be used.

reviewed_sources.title: On the Importance of Accurate Relative Motion Models for Target Vehicle Trajectory Tracking
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Alai et al. - 2024 - On the Importance of Accurate Relative Motion Models for Target Vehicle Trajectory Tracking.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pp1-6 including sensor alternatives, simulations, EKF experimental section and conclusions; garbled extracted equations require visual check.
findings: Eqs11-16 derive body-frame relative motion with rotation terms from ego translation/yaw; requires ego velocity and yaw rate, not global ego position/yaw. Mixed relative and absolute state.
Constant target acceleration and slowly changing/constant target sideslip kinematic assumptions. Low-cost ego velocity options Sec3 have additional kinematic/tire-slip/bias limitations.

Experiments use EKF with radar,IMU,speedometer. Does not itself prove deterministic joint estimator-controller collision safety. Affects attribution: cite Alai etal2024 for relative model and Sharma etal2026 for multistage observer.

reviewed_sources.title: Nonlinear Coordinated Steering and Braking Control of Vision-Based Autonomous Vehicles in Emergency Obstacle Avoidance
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Guo et al. - 2016 - Nonlinear Coordinated Steering and Braking Control of Vision-Based Autonomous Vehicles in Emergency.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pages1-11 including complete main body, displayed derivations, results, conclusion and references.
findings: Printedp3231 discusses kinematic, tire-force and load-transfer coupling; its actual reduced model ignores vertical,roll,pitch motion, so do not claim all listed mechanisms are modeled.
Eqs1-3 retain body cross-axis dynamics and steering contributions. Eq36 jointly determines brake pressure and steering; coordinated versus separate LTV-steering/SMC-braking field comparison.
Theorem1 tracking statement and proof ultimate-bound calculation are not collision-free invariance certificates. Existing coordinated emergency avoidance work defeats a first-to-couple claim.

reviewed_sources.title: Coupled lateral-longitudinal vehicle dynamics and control design with three-dimensional state portraits
reviewed_sources.original_pdf_filename: Beal and Boyd - 2019 - Coupled lateral-longitudinal vehicle dynamics and control design with three-dimensional state portra.pdf
reviewed_sources.coverage: Full original PDF pages1-29 including complete main body, displayed derivations, results, conclusion and references.
findings: Section2 Eqs1-6 retains variable longitudinal speed,four-wheel force projection,nonlinear slip and coupled brush tire forces. Full29-page early-access PDF includes cover; online2018, subsequently volume57(2),pages286-313.

Section3.2 state-dependent available derivative directions and braking trajectories illustrate limits of constant-speed analysis. Section3.3 validates one operating-curve representation, not all initial states.

Section5 explicitly says state portraits do not prove stability. Hierarchical critical-cornering example jointly selects steering/braking under input constraints; hierarchy does not imply ignored physical coupling. Actuator bandwidth omitted in simulated example.

coupling_addendum.independent_calculation: Ideal isotropic tire friction circle: longitudinal utilization0.8 leaves lateral capacity sqrt(1-0.8^2)=0.6; independent0.8 component requests have combined utilization sqrt(1.28)>1. No simulation.
coupling_addendum.scope_decision: Criticize ignored or uncoordinated coupling within the claimed operating domain; do not equate hierarchical or separate-module control with decoupled physical modeling. Coupling alone is not novel.
code_findings: Fiala branch retains cross-axis dynamics,front force projection and longitudinal-ratio-dependent lateral saturation; per-hold optimization contains both inputs.
Low-speed kinematic branch/blend has different model scope; wheel inertia/dynamic normal-load effects are reduced-model residuals.
Solver explicitly has no steering magnitude/slew limit; joint optimization does not imply every physical actuator limit is enforced.
coupling_addendum.validation: Read-only algorithm inspection; no new complete-controller theory audit or experiment.
